traveler: Mao Zedong (Mao Tse-tung), Chairman of the Communist Party of China
title: From Shaoshan to the Crystal Case: the Long March, the Cave Years, and the Founding of the People's Republic
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Village and the Normal School

stops.name: Shaoshan, birth in the mud-brick house
stops.campa: In a mud-brick farmhouse under the hills of Shaoshan, in the nineteenth year of the Guangxu emperor, a son is born to Mao Yichang, a grain dealer who climbed out of debt into twenty-two mou of land, and to Wen Qimei, who keeps the Buddhist observances her husband despises. The Qing dynasty has eighteen years left. The village lies fifty kilometres from Changsha over bad roads, and nothing in it has changed in the lifetime of anyone living in it. The boy is put to field work at six and to the Confucian classics at eight, and he hates his father.
suggested_refs: The Mao family farmhouse at Shaoshan, preserved as a national memorial site
sources: Edgar Snow, Red Star Over China (1937)

stops.name: Shaoshan, the marriage he refuses
stops.date_confidence: contested: Wikipedia's 'Mao Zedong' puts the arranged marriage at age 13 with Luo Yixiu aged 17; the dedicated 'Luo Yixiu' article gives 1908, Mao aged 14, Luo aged 18. Dated here to 1907 with the window 1907-1908 left open.
stops.campa: His father contracts him to Luo Yixiu of the neighbouring Luo clan, some four years his elder, and the wedding is held in the Mao house. The boy refuses to recognize it. He will not live with her, and in later life he does not count her among his wives; the village counts her anyway, and she keeps the name. She dies of dysentery at twenty, in 1910, in the house of a husband who would not have her. Her grave is at Shaoshan. The pilgrims who come to the birthplace by the busload a century later are not shown it.
suggested_refs: The Luo family graves at Shaoshan, outside the memorial circuit

stops.name: Dongshan school, Xiangxiang, the walk out of the village
stops.campa: Sixteen years old, seventeen by his own country's reckoning, he walks out of Shaoshan against his father's will with his bedroll on his back, to the Dongshan Higher Primary School in the next county, where the sons of landlords mock his cotton clothes and his Xiangtan accent. He reads there of Washington and Napoleon and Peter the Great, of the reformers Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao, and learns that China is a country and that other countries exist. He tells Edgar Snow, a quarter of a century afterward, that a pamphlet on the partition of China made him weep.
suggested_refs: Dongshan Higher Primary School, Xiangxiang county, first school outside Shaoshan
sources: Edgar Snow, Red Star Over China (1937), Mao's autobiographical account

stops.name: Changsha, the republic and the soldier
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year; the month of his enlistment is not fixed in the reachable sources
stops.campa: He reaches the provincial capital in the spring and is there in October when the Wuchang rising brings the Qing down. He cuts off his queue, enlists as a private in the Hunan revolutionary army, and serves six months, paying a water carrier to fetch his water on the grounds that a student does not carry water. In the same weeks Hermann Keyserling lands at Canton and finds the empire already fallen, and goes on to Tsingtao to sit with the exiled mandarin Ku Hung-ming among the wreckage of a civilisation gathered in villas.
suggested_refs: The Hunan New Army barracks at Changsha, where Mao served six months in 1911-1912
sources: Edgar Snow, Red Star Over China (1937)

stops.name: Hunan First Normal School, Changsha
stops.date_confidence: enrolment attested to spring 1913; the graduation date is contested. Wikipedia's 'Mao Zedong' says June 1919, which contradicts the same article's placing him in Beijing from autumn 1918; Short, Spence, and Pantsov and Levine give June 1918, ranked third in his year.
stops.campa: He enrols at the Fourth Normal School of Changsha, folded the following year into the First Normal School of Hunan, and stays five years. He reads Adam Smith and Rousseau and Darwin alongside the classics, publishes his first article in New Youth on physical education, arguing that a nation of weak bodies cannot make a revolution, and bathes in cold rivers in November to prove the point on himself. With Cai Hesen he founds the Renovation of the People Study Society, seventy or eighty members, most of them students, a good many of them dead within the decade.
suggested_refs: Hunan First Normal School, Changsha, preserved as a memorial site

stops.name: Peking University library, Beijing: the clerk at the desk
stops.campa: Yang Changji, his old teacher, gets him a post as assistant to the librarian Li Dazhao at Peking University, registering the names of readers for eight silver dollars a month. The great men of the New Culture Movement come to his desk and do not stop to talk to a Hunanese clerk with a provincial accent. He reads anarchist pamphlets and the first Chinese accounts of the Russian revolution. Marco Polo entered this city as Khanbaliq and was given office in it; Matteo Ricci died here in 1610 and lies at Zhalan, a few li west. Mao is refused a conversation.
suggested_refs: The old Peking University library at Shatan, Li Dazhao's reading room
sources: Edgar Snow, Red Star Over China (1937)

stops.name: Changsha, the Xiang River Review
stops.campa: He is not in Beijing on the fourth of May; he left for Shanghai in the spring, and he takes up the movement from Hunan instead. In July he founds and edits the Xiang River Review, writing most of it himself, and the warlord governor Zhang Jingyao shuts it down after five issues. In December he organizes a general strike of students and a delegation to Beijing demanding Zhang's removal, and helps found the Hunanese Student Association. Zhang is removed.
suggested_refs: Surviving issues of the Xiang River Review, Changsha, July-August 1919

stops.name: Changsha, marriage to Yang Kaihui
stops.date_confidence: traditional: the year is attested, the month is conventional
stops.campa: He marries Yang Kaihui, daughter of the teacher who died that January in Beijing. She is nineteen and refuses a conventional wedding. He is appointed headmaster of the junior section of the First Normal School and turns the salary into a bookshop, the Cultural Book Society, and into a Self-Study University teaching classics and Marxism in the same rooms. She bears him three sons. In 1930 the Kuomintang will take her at Changsha and offer her life in exchange for a public renunciation of her husband, and she will refuse it, and be shot at twenty-nine.
suggested_refs: The Cultural Book Society premises, Changsha; the Yang Kaihui memorial at Bancang

stops.name: Shanghai, the house in the French Concession
stops.campa: Thirteen men meet in a girls' school in the French Concession to found a party, with two Comintern agents in attendance. Mao, twenty-seven, is one of two delegates from Hunan and is given the minutes to keep; he says little, and what he says is not recorded in full. The organization they are constituting has between fifty and sixty members in the whole of China. Of the thirteen in the room, most will leave the party, defect to the Japanese, or be executed by one side or the other. Two of them will be standing on the Tiananmen rostrum in 1949.
suggested_refs: The First Congress site at Xintiandi, Shanghai, now a national museum
sources: Wikipedia, '1st National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party'

stops.name: South Lake, Jiaxing: the congress finished on a boat
stops.campa: A stranger walks into the meeting room and leaves without explaining himself; the delegates scatter within minutes, and Concession police search the house. They reconvene on a pleasure boat hired on South Lake at Jiaxing, a woman posing as a passenger to watch the shore, mahjong tiles laid out on the table to be rattled if anyone approaches. On the water they adopt the programme and elect a three-man bureau. The boat is now a relic of the state; a replica is moored at the spot, and schoolchildren are brought by the coachload to look at it.
suggested_refs: The Red Boat replica on South Lake, Jiaxing, Zhejiang
sources: Wikipedia, '1st National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party'

stops.name: Guangzhou, the Peasant Movement Training Institute
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1926; the exact opening date of the sixth term is not fixed here
stops.campa: Under the united front with the Kuomintang, and as an alternate member of its Central Executive Committee, he runs the sixth term of the Peasant Movement Training Institute in a converted Confucian temple in Canton: students from twenty provinces, rifle drill in the mornings, rural survey work in the afternoons. The doctrine he teaches here is the one nobody senior in his own party wants, that the revolution will be made by peasants rather than by the thin industrial working class of the coast. Ibn Battuta described this city's mosque and its potters six centuries before.
suggested_refs: The Peasant Movement Training Institute, Guangzhou, preserved in the former Confucian temple

stops.name: Hunan, the report on the peasant movement
stops.campa: He spends thirty-two days walking through five counties of his own province while the peasant associations there swell past two million members, dragging landlords through the streets in tall paper hats and holding their own courts. He writes down what he sees and refuses to apologize for any of it. The report appears in March, weeks before Chiang Kai-shek's men begin killing Communists in the streets of Shanghai. Its central passage is addressed to the comrades in the cities who complain that the peasants have gone too far.
stops.quote: A revolution is not a dinner party, or writing an essay, or painting a picture, or doing embroidery; it cannot be so refined, so leisurely and gentle, so temperate, kind, courteous, restrained and magnanimous. A revolution is an insurrection, an act of violence by which one class overthrows another.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan (March 1927), Selected Works vol. I, section 'The Question of Going Too Far'
suggested_refs: Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan, March 1927
sources: Mao Zedong, Selected Works vol. I, via marxists.org (text verified by direct fetch)

stops.name: Nanchang, the uprising he is not at
stops.campa: Four months after Chiang turns on the united front, Communist officers seize Nanchang before dawn: Zhou Enlai directing as secretary of the Front Committee, He Long commanding in chief, Ye Ting leading the main force, Zhu De a subordinate unit. They hold the city five days and are driven out of it. The date becomes the birthday of the Red Army and is stamped on its flags for the next century. Mao is not there. He is in Hunan preparing a rising of his own, and the army founded this morning will be under his hand within eight years.
suggested_refs: The Nanchang Uprising Memorial Hall, former Jiangxi Grand Hotel headquarters

stops.name: Wenjiashi, Liuyang: the turn toward the hills
stops.campa: The Autumn Harvest Uprising fails in ten days. Four regiments of miners, deserters and peasants move on Changsha, are beaten separately on the way, and converge on the town of Wenjiashi on the Jiangxi border with perhaps a thousand men left out of five thousand. In the hall of the Lishen school Mao argues against a second attempt on the city and for the mountains instead. The front committee votes with him. The party strips him of his Politburo seat for the defeat, and he turns south with the survivors toward country no government has ever governed.
suggested_refs: The Lishen school hall at Wenjiashi, Liuyang, site of the 19-20 September 1927 meeting

stops.name: Sanwan, Yongxin: the party inside the company
stops.campa: At the village of Sanwan he takes the remnant apart and rebuilds it: one regiment where a division had been, officers forbidden to beat the men, a soldiers' committee in every company, and a party branch at company level whose secretary answers upward through the party and not through the chain of command. Any man who wants to go is given travelling money at the gate. Six hundred stay. Party branches at company level are still written into the regulations of the People's Liberation Army.
suggested_refs: The Sanwan Reorganization site, Yongxin county, Jiangxi

stops.name: Jinggangshan (Ciping), the first base
stops.campa: He leads them up into the Jinggang Mountains on the Hunan and Jiangxi border, five great ridges and one road in, and makes terms with the two bandit chiefs who hold the passes, Yuan Wencai and Wang Zuo: their men into his army, his doctors and rifles into their villages. Land is redistributed, peasants are taught characters, and the force reaches about eighteen hundred. In April Zhu De arrives with the survivors of Nanchang, Lin Biao among them, and the Fourth Red Army is formed. The tactics are set down here in sixteen characters, beginning with the enemy advances, we retreat.
suggested_refs: The Ciping base and the Jinggangshan Revolutionary Museum
sources: Edgar Snow, Red Star Over China (1937)

stops.name: Ruijin, the Chinese Soviet Republic
stops.campa: On the anniversary of the October Revolution a Chinese Soviet Republic is proclaimed at Ruijin in southern Jiangxi: its own currency, post office, land law and marriage law, governing some three million people in a pocket of hill country. Mao is its chairman, and from this year onward he is called Chairman Mao. Real command passes over his head to the students returned from Moscow and to Otto Braun, sent by the Comintern, who meets Chiang's fifth encirclement campaign with fortified lines and blockhouse warfare and loses the base doing it.
suggested_refs: The Chinese Soviet Republic government buildings at Ruijin, Jiangxi

stops.name: Yudu, the river crossed at night
stops.campa: Eighty-six thousand soldiers and cadres cross the Yudu river after dark on pontoon bridges made of doors and fishing boats, the bridges laid at dusk and lifted again before first light so the aircraft find bare water. They carry the printing press, the mint, an X-ray machine, and the archives of a republic. Nobody is told where they are going, because nobody has decided; the working plan is to reach the Second and Sixth Army Groups in Hunan. Mao travels sick with malaria on a litter, out of favour, holding no command. The wounded are left in the villages.
suggested_refs: The Yudu river crossing points, Jiangxi, marked as the Long March departure site

stops.name: Xiang River, Guangxi: the fourth blockade line
stops.date_confidence: attested to 30 November-1 December 1934; the wider battle window in Wikipedia's 'Long March' runs later into December
stops.campa: The fourth blockade line is the Xiang, and the Guangxi and Hunan armies hold both banks of it. The crossing at the Jieshou ferry takes five days because the column is strung out over eighty kilometres, dragging its furniture behind it. When the rearguard is finally over, eighty-six thousand have become thirty-six thousand. The heavy equipment goes into the water. The disaster destroys what authority Bo Gu and Otto Braun still had, and the officers who blame them begin, on the road, to talk to one another about Mao.
suggested_refs: The Jieshou ferry site and the Xiang River battlefields of Xing'an, Quanzhou and Guanyang counties

stops.name: Zunyi, the meeting in the merchant's house
stops.date_confidence: contested: traditionally dated 7-9 January 1935; dated here to 15-17 January following Fei Peiru's revision, which Wikipedia's 'Zunyi Conference' adopts
stops.campa: In a two-storey merchant's house with a European balcony, twenty men sit for three days over the wreck of the campaign. Mao speaks longest and has the arithmetic of the Xiang on his side. Bo Gu and Otto Braun are removed from military command, Mao is put on the standing committee and made Zhou Enlai's assistant in military affairs, and the line that lost Jiangxi is disowned by the men who followed it. Party history dates his leadership from this room. Zhou Enlai, for the moment, is still the man who signs the orders.
suggested_refs: The Zunyi Conference site, Guizhou, preserved as a museum

stops.name: Jiaopingdu, the Jinsha crossed on seven boats
stops.date_confidence: attested for the crossing window 29 April-9 May 1935; the exact ferry coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: He walks the army four times back and forth across the Chishui, feints at Guiyang until Chiang Kai-shek flies there in person to take charge, then marches west into Yunnan and swings north for the Jinsha, the upper Yangtze, where no one is waiting. At the Jiaopingdu ferry seven boats carry the whole First Front Army over in nine days and nights, the ferrymen working in shifts around the clock, the boats burned on the far bank. The pursuit arrives to find no crossing left.
suggested_refs: The Jiaopingdu ferry between Luquan county, Yunnan, and Huili county, Sichuan

stops.name: Luding Bridge, the chains over the Dadu
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date; the scale of the action is contested. Wikipedia's 'Battle of Luding Bridge' carries the canonical account, which Sun Shuyun's field interviews along the route dispute.
stops.campa: Thirteen iron chains slung across the Dadu gorge in 1706, the planking stripped off them, a machine gun in the tower on the far side. Twenty-two volunteers go hand over hand along the chains with grenades in their belts, and the army crosses behind them, and the Dadu does not become the river where the Red Army ends as the Taiping ended on it seventy years earlier. The canon holds it exactly so. Sun Shuyun, walking the route with a notebook two generations later, found villagers who remembered no battle at the bridge at all.
suggested_refs: The Luding chain bridge, Sichuan, built 1706, and the Long March memorial beside it
sources: Sun Shuyun's field interviews as cited in Western accounts

stops.name: Lazikou Pass, Gansu: the last gorge
stops.date_confidence: attested: vanguard arrives 16 September 1935, main assault 17 September, position cleared 18 September, per the Chinese Wikipedia article on the Lazikou campaign. The coordinate is approximate; the pass lies northeast of Diebu county town in Gannan.
stops.campa: A gorge thirty metres wide in the Min Shan, held from blockhouses above the only path. The vanguard reaches it on the sixteenth of September and cannot force it head on; a detachment climbs the cliff in the dark and drops grenades onto the works from above, and by the morning of the eighteenth the pass is open. It is the last mountain barrier on the road. Beyond it the loess plateau of the northwest begins, and somewhere out in it, though nobody in the column yet knows this, a Communist base is still standing.
suggested_refs: The Lazikou pass in the Min Shan, Diebu (Tewo) county, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture

stops.name: Wuqizhen, Shaanxi: the end of the march
stops.campa: The column walks into the market town of Wuqizhen in northern Shaanxi with something between six and eight thousand men, out of the eighty-six thousand who left Jiangxi a year and three days before. They have covered around nine thousand kilometres, crossed eighteen mountain ranges and twenty-four rivers, and lost the rest of the army to battle, cold, marsh, hunger and desertion. Yan'an is a hundred and forty-five kilometres off and still in other hands. Mao writes a poem about the Liupan mountains on the way in.
suggested_refs: Wuqizhen, Wuqi county, Shaanxi, terminus of the First Front Army's Long March

stops.name: Wayaobao, Zichang: the united front line
stops.campa: At Wayaobao, in the county town of Zichang, the Politburo meets for nine days and turns the party's face away from civil war and toward Japan. The line adopted is the anti-Japanese national united front: landlords, capitalists, and the Kuomintang itself are to be courted against the invader. The men who vote it through walked out of Jiangxi fourteen months earlier with eighty-six thousand and arrived with eight thousand. Within ten years the party has more than a million members.
suggested_refs: The Wayaobao Conference site at Wayaobu, Zichang, Shaanxi

stops.name: Xi'an, the generalissimo arrested
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Incident (12-25 December 1936); the Second United Front itself is announced in September 1937
stops.campa: Zhang Xueliang, whose Manchuria the Japanese hold and whose troops Chiang Kai-shek has ordered against the Communists instead, arrests his own commander in chief at the Huaqing hot springs outside Xi'an and holds him thirteen days. Zhou Enlai negotiates for the party; Moscow instructs that Chiang be kept alive. He is released on Christmas Day, and a second united front follows in September. Athanasius Kircher printed this city's Nestorian stele in Rome in 1667 and read it as proof that China had been Christian and forgotten it.
suggested_refs: The Huaqing Pool site outside Xi'an, where Chiang was seized in December 1936

stops.name: Yan'an, the lectures on contradiction
stops.campa: The party takes Yan'an in the winter and Mao begins lecturing at the Anti-Japanese Military and Political University on dialectics, reading the Soviet textbooks a few weeks ahead of his students. On Practice and On Contradiction are worked up out of these lectures. In a town of cave dwellings cut into loess cliffs he is writing a philosophy with a Chinese name on it. Cadres walk in from the coastal cities by the thousand, take the course, and are sent back out carrying it.
stops.quote: The law of contradiction in things, that is, the law of the unity of opposites, is the basic law of materialist dialectics.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, On Contradiction (August 1937), Selected Works vol. I
suggested_refs: On Practice and On Contradiction, written at Yan'an in 1937
sources: Mao Zedong, Selected Works vol. I, via marxists.org (text verified by direct fetch)

stops.name: Yangjialing, Yan'an: the barrel of the gun
stops.campa: At the close of the sixth plenum of the Sixth Central Committee, with the Japanese holding Wuhan and Canton and the war settled into its long middle, he states the relation of the party to the army in a formula that will be recited for the next ninety years and cast in bronze on parade grounds. Eleven years earlier at Sanwan he had put party branches inside the rifle companies, watched by six hundred men who were offered travelling money at the gate and stayed.
stops.quote: Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun. Our principle is that the Party commands the gun, and the gun must never be allowed to command the Party.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, Problems of War and Strategy (6 November 1938), Selected Works vol. II
suggested_refs: Problems of War and Strategy, closing speech to the sixth plenum, Yan'an
sources: Mao Zedong, Selected Works vol. II, via marxists.org (text verified by direct fetch)

stops.name: Yan'an, He Zizhen leaves and Jiang Qing arrives
stops.campa: He Zizhen came out of Jinggangshan and walked the whole march to Shaanxi. She bore children on the road and left them with peasants; the shrapnel from a strafing is still in her body. In the autumn of 1937 she goes to Moscow and does not come back in time. That marriage is never formally dissolved. In November of the following year Mao marries Lan Ping, a Shanghai film actress arrived in Yan'an with a stage name and a complicated history, who now calls herself Jiang Qing. The Politburo consents on condition that she stay out of politics for twenty years. She keeps to it, and then does not.
suggested_refs: The Yan'an cave residences of the Mao household, 1937-1947

stops.name: Zaoyuan, Yan'an: rectification, and Mount Tai
stops.date_confidence: attested for the speech; the Rectification Movement runs from 1942 and the chairmanship is confirmed 20 March 1943
stops.campa: From the courtyard at Zaoyuan he runs the Rectification Movement: study circles, criticism and self-criticism, confessions extracted by Kang Sheng's security men until cadres are killing themselves, and at the end of it a party that thinks in his vocabulary and no other. In March 1943 he is made chairman of the Politburo and of the secretariat, with power to overrule both. In September 1944 he speaks at a memorial for Zhang Side, a soldier of the guard regiment crushed when a charcoal kiln caved in on him.
stops.quote: Though death befalls all men alike, it may be weightier than Mount Tai or lighter than a feather.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, Serve the People (8 September 1944), Selected Works vol. III
suggested_refs: The Zaoyuan compound, Yan'an; the text of Serve the People, September 1944
sources: Mao Zedong, Selected Works vol. III, via marxists.org (text verified by direct fetch)

stops.name: Yangjialing, the Seventh Party Congress
stops.date_confidence: attested (the congress sat from 23 April to 11 June 1945)
stops.campa: Seven hundred and fifty-five delegates meet in a barn-roofed hall at Yangjialing for fifty days, the first party congress in seventeen years. The constitution they adopt names Mao Zedong Thought as the guide for all the party's work, the first time a living Chinese Communist is written into the founding document as a source of doctrine. The party has one million two hundred thousand members and an army near a million. Ten years earlier it had eight thousand men walking into a market town in Shaanxi.
suggested_refs: The Seventh Congress hall at Yangjialing, Yan'an

stops.name: Chongqing, forty-three days with Chiang
stops.campa: He flies into the Nationalist wartime capital under American escort, with Ambassador Patrick Hurley in the aircraft as a hostage for his safety, and stays forty-three days negotiating with Chiang Kai-shek face to face for the first time in eighteen years. They raise glasses to each other in front of photographers. The agreement signed on the tenth of October settles nothing that matters, and both armies are moving while it is being drafted. In Chongqing he publishes the poem Snow, which measures the emperors of the past and finds every one of them short.
suggested_refs: The Guiyuan house, Chongqing, where the 1945 negotiations were held

stops.name: Xibaipo, Hebei: the war run from a courtyard
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1948; the Central Committee leaves in March 1949
stops.campa: From a courtyard in a Hebei village of a hundred households, with the telegraph office in the next room, he directs the three campaigns that finish the war: Liaoshen, Huaihai, Pingjin, a million and a half Nationalist troops destroyed or surrendered in four months. The Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee meets here in March 1949 and rules that the centre of the party's work moves from the village to the city. He tells the delegates they are going up to Beijing to sit the imperial examinations, and that they must not come back having failed them.
suggested_refs: The Xibaipo memorial site, Pingshan county, Shijiazhuang, Hebei

segments.name: The Chairman of the New State

stops.name: Tiananmen Gate, the proclamation of the People's Republic
stops.campa: At three in the afternoon he stands on the rostrum of the Gate of Heavenly Peace, above the portrait of himself, and reads out the founding of the People's Republic of China in a Hunanese the crowd below cannot entirely follow. Genghis Khan's Mongols burned Zhongdu on this ground through the winter of 1215; Marco Polo was received here when the city was Khanbaliq; Matteo Ricci died here in 1610 and was granted ground for his grave inside the Middle Kingdom. The city has been a capital under four dynasties and is one again by nightfall.
suggested_refs: The Tiananmen rostrum and the newsreel of the 1 October 1949 proclamation

stops.name: The Kremlin, Moscow: the first journey abroad
stops.campa: His first journey outside China, at fifty-six, is a nine-day train to Moscow for Stalin's seventieth birthday. He is installed in a dacha and left in it for weeks, granted two audiences, and complains to his hosts that he has not come all this way to eat and sleep. The Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance is signed on the fourteenth of February 1950: three hundred million dollars of credit over five years, at one per cent, for a country of five hundred million people.
suggested_refs: The Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance, 14 February 1950

stops.name: Pyongyang, the volunteers across the Yalu
stops.date_confidence: attested for the first crossing of the Chinese People's Volunteers
stops.campa: Chinese People's Volunteers cross the Yalu at night in October and push MacArthur's armies back from the Chinese border to the thirty-eighth parallel over the winter, at a price that includes Mao's eldest son Mao Anying, killed by napalm at a command post in November. He refuses to have the body brought home and it stays in Korean ground. Twenty-three years later Isabel Peron flies the Beijing to Pyongyang circuit as a state guest, received here by Kim Il-sung four days after Beijing received her, on a road this war opened.
suggested_refs: The grave of Mao Anying at the Chinese People's Volunteers cemetery, Hoechang, North Korea

stops.name: Zhongnanhai, Beijing: chairman of the state
stops.date_confidence: attested for the election under the new constitution
stops.campa: He lives inside the walled lake garden west of the Forbidden City, in a study where half the bed is occupied by books, and he leaves it mainly for trains and for swimming. In September 1954 the first National People's Congress makes him Chairman of the People's Republic under the new constitution. By then land reform has killed somewhere between one and two million landlords, the Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries has run its course, and the private economy of the coastal cities is being taken into the state ward by ward.
suggested_refs: The Chrysanthemum Fragrance Study, Mao's residence inside Zhongnanhai

stops.name: Beijing, the hundred flowers and what grew
stops.date_confidence: attested for the speech; the Hundred Flowers Campaign opens in 1956 and the Anti-Rightist Campaign follows from mid-1957
stops.campa: In 1956 he invites the intellectuals to speak: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend. They speak, and what they say about the party is a good deal worse than anyone inside Zhongnanhai had budgeted for. The Anti-Rightist Campaign follows within months, and something near half a million of them go to labour camps, to the villages, or out of their professions for good. He had set out the doctrine in February, at the Supreme State Conference, distinguishing contradictions among the people from contradictions with the enemy.
stops.quote: Contradictions exist everywhere, but their nature differs in accordance with the different nature of different things.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People (27 February 1957), Selected Works vol. V
suggested_refs: On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People, speech to the Supreme State Conference, 27 February 1957
sources: Mao Zedong, Selected Works vol. V, via marxists.org (text verified by direct fetch)

stops.name: The Kremlin, Moscow: the east wind
stops.campa: He returns to Moscow for the fortieth anniversary of the October Revolution and the conference of sixty-four Communist parties, his second journey abroad and his last. Sputnik is a month old. He tells the delegates that the east wind prevails over the west wind, and, in a passage the Russians repeat afterwards with alarm, that China could lose three hundred million people in a nuclear war and have three hundred million left. Khrushchev dates the split from this visit. Che Guevara arraigns the same Soviet bloc at Algiers in 1965.
suggested_refs: The 1957 Moscow Conference of Communist and Workers' Parties

stops.name: Shaoshan, the homecoming
stops.campa: He comes back to the village for the first time in thirty-two years, sleeps at the guest house near Dishuidong, and walks up the hill at first light to his parents' grave with a handful of pine branches, having brought nothing else. He eats with old neighbours and asks how the communal kitchens are feeding people, and they tell him what he has come to hear. That night he writes a poem about the red flag and the whips of the landlords. The famine begun by his Great Leap Forward is in its first year and will kill tens of millions.
suggested_refs: The Dishuidong guest house at Shaoshan and the graves of Mao Yichang and Wen Qimei

stops.name: Lushan, Jiangxi: Peng Dehuai's letter
stops.date_confidence: attested (the Lushan conference ran July to August 1959)
stops.campa: The leadership goes up into the cool of the Lushan resort to correct the excesses of the Leap, and Peng Dehuai, minister of defence, commander in Korea, a peasant like Mao and a blunter man, hands him a private letter setting out what he has seen in the villages. Mao has the letter printed and circulated to the whole plenum and requires the party to choose between them. It chooses him. Peng is dismissed as a right opportunist, the Leap is redoubled rather than corrected, and the two worst years of the famine follow directly out of this meeting.
suggested_refs: The Lushan conference villas, Jiangxi, and the text of Peng Dehuai's July 1959 letter

segments.name: The Cultural Revolution and the Crystal Case

stops.name: The Yangtze at Wuhan, the swim
stops.campa: Seventy-two years old, months out of Beijing, rumoured ill and rumoured finished, he goes into the Yangtze at Wuhan in front of the cameras and comes down fifteen kilometres of brown current in sixty-five minutes, a speed the river explains and the newspapers decline to. Photographs of the head above the water run on every front page in China. He is back in the capital inside the month and the Cultural Revolution begins in earnest. The Eleventh Plenum meets three weeks later and drops Liu Shaoqi from second in the party to eighth.
suggested_refs: Press photographs of the 16 July 1966 Yangtze swim at Wuhan

stops.name: Tiananmen rostrum, the Red Guard rallies
stops.date_confidence: attested (eight rallies between August and November 1966)
stops.campa: From the same rostrum, eight times between August and November, he reviews the Red Guards: eleven or twelve million of them brought to Beijing by free rail, filling the square from before dawn, weeping, holding up the little red book the army newspaper compiled in 1964 and which will be printed past a billion copies in four years. A schoolgirl of the Beijing Normal girls' school, Song Binbin, whose name means refined, pins an armband on his sleeve. Be martial, he tells her. She renames herself Song Yaowu, and her school's headmistress is beaten to death that month.
stops.quote: Marxism comprises many principles, but in the final analysis they can all be brought back to a single sentence: it is right to rebel.
stops.quote_source: Mao Zedong, speech at the Yan'an rally for Stalin's sixtieth birthday, 20 December 1939, per Wikiquote (tertiary sourcing; not held on marxists.org). Revised in 1966-1967 Red Guard usage to the slogan form 'It is right to rebel against reactionaries'.
suggested_refs: Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung, first compiled 5 January 1964 by the People's Liberation Army Daily

stops.name: Zhongnanhai, the death of the Chairman
stops.campa: He dies at ten minutes past midnight, eighty-two years old, having outlived Zhou Enlai by eight months and Zhu De by two, in a year that also brought the Tangshan earthquake and its quarter of a million dead, which is the kind of conjunction the dynastic histories were written to record. He had signed a pledge in favour of cremation, as party policy required. Within four weeks Jiang Qing and three others are under arrest and the Cultural Revolution is declared to be over. He had been chairman of the party for thirty-three years.
suggested_refs: Building 202, Zhongnanhai, where Mao died on 9 September 1976
sources: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Mao Zedong'

stops.name: Mao Zedong Memorial Hall, Tiananmen Square
stops.date_confidence: attested for completion; construction began 24 November 1976
stops.campa: The body goes to the 305 Hospital on the seventeenth of September, the organs are taken out and kept in formaldehyde, and Wang Dongxing organizes an embalming that nobody in the country has done before. A mausoleum is raised on Tiananmen Square between November and May, on the razed foundations of the old Gate of China, and he is laid in a crystal case inside it, facing the rostrum he proclaimed the republic from. The queue forms before the doors open. Some of the people standing in it say the figure is wax.
suggested_refs: The Chairman Mao Memorial Hall, Tiananmen Square, opened 24 May 1977
sources: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Mao Zedong'
